news.headline: Federal judge blocks FCC's early review of ABC broadcast licenses
news.summary: U.S. District Judge Loren AliKhan granted a preliminary injunction halting the FCC's early renewal review of ABC's broadcast licenses, citing First Amendment concerns. The ruling involves ABC, Disney, the FCC and a judge appointed during the Biden administration. It limits the agency's action and raises questions about regulatory oversight and free‑speech protections.

news.headline: Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade postponed due to severe weather
news.summary: A nor'easter moving up the East Coast prompted organizers to delay the Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade in New York City to Saturday. The decision was made after consultations with city officials and the police department, citing safety concerns for participants and spectators. The postponement affects the parade's 100th anniversary celebration and its iconic balloon segment.

news.headline: Trump calls revised Q3 GDP figures 'fake' and seeks investigation
news.summary: President Donald Trump alleged that the government deliberately under‑reported third‑quarter GDP before the midterm elections and demanded a probe into the Commerce Department's data revision. The Bureau of Economic Analysis later revised the estimate upward by about 0.9 percentage points. Trump posted the claim on Truth Social without providing evidence. The controversy highlights partisan tensions over economic statistics during an election cycle.

news.headline: White House chief of staff Stephen Miller leads response to Iowa Army detonation
news.summary: The U.S. Army detonated a large quantity of lead azide in Iowa, prompting a communications effort by the White House. Chief of staff Stephen Miller coordinated the response and was publicly praised by some officials. The incident is being watched as a test of the administration's handling of environmental and safety issues. It also highlights internal dynamics within the Trump administration.

news.headline: Trump and NATO chief meet at Mar-a-Lago, urge Russia to avoid expanding Ukraine war
news.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump met with NATO Secretary‑General Jens Stoltenberg at Mar‑a‑Lago and issued a joint statement urging Russia not to broaden its military actions in Ukraine. The meeting was highlighted by both sides as a diplomatic outreach, while NATO officials emphasized Ukraine's strong defense. The encounter comes amid ongoing debate over U.S. policy toward Russia and support for Ukraine.

news.headline: Elon Musk announces two SpaceX shares for every American child via Trump Accounts
news.summary: SpaceX and CEO Elon Musk said they will issue two shares of Class A common stock to each American child who has an active Trump Account. The company will provide one share and Musk will match it with a personal share. The pledge follows a similar commitment made last month and is presented as a charitable giveaway. The distribution will be handled through the tax‑advantaged Trump Accounts created for children in the United States.

news.headline: FAA briefly halts departures at Chicago O'Hare due to equipment outage
news.summary: The Federal Aviation Administration issued a short‑lived ground stop at Chicago O'Hare International Airport on Tuesday afternoon, citing an equipment outage with a ground surveillance radar system. The pause, lifted by 4:15 p.m. CST, delayed dozens of flights during the peak Thanksgiving travel period. The incident highlights the challenges of maintaining air‑traffic operations during a major holiday travel surge.

news.headline: Denny's reinstates plaque honoring Nvidia founder Jensen Huang after his return as CEO
news.summary: Denny's announced it has restored a commemorative plaque at its San Jose location marking the booth where Jensen Huang and co‑founders conceived Nvidia in 1993. The plaque was removed earlier amid controversy surrounding Huang's resignation and allegations of an affair with a Chinese spy. The restaurant's decision follows Huang's reinstatement as Nvidia CEO. The move highlights the intersection of corporate branding and political scrutiny.

news.headline: U.S. Army Reschedules Lead Azide Detonation at Iowa Ammunition Plant
news.summary: The U.S. Army announced that it will conduct a controlled detonation of more than 60 barrels of degraded lead azide at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant on Wednesday, Nov. 25. The schedule change follows a federal court order that placed an indefinite pause on the operation and ongoing debate over public health and safety. President Trump has said the final decision will depend on court approval and the incoming Iowa governor. The Army says the timing is set to take advantage of optimal weather conditions.

news.headline: Steelers bench veteran quarterback Aaron Rodgers amid coach-player clash
news.summary: The Pittsburgh Steelers announced that starting quarterback Aaron Rodgers will not play, naming Mason Rudolph as the starter for the upcoming game. Coach Mike McCarthy cited disagreements over the offense as the reason for the benching. Rodgers responded with a heated interview accusing the coach of unprofessional behavior. The move raises questions about Rodgers' future with the team and the franchise's direction.

satire.headline: Trump Announces Thanksgiving Turkey Won't Be Pardoned, Will Face Firing Squad
satire.summary: WASHINGTON D.C. – President Trump today pardoned a Thanksgiving turkey, after the bird had apparently donated over $4.2 million dollars directly to the Trump family via their World Liberty Financial cryptocurrency exchange. WASHINGTON, D.C. — President Donald Trump announced today that this year's Thanksgiving Turkey will not be pardoned and will instead face execution by a firing squad.

Zoom Introduces New Virtual Hair Feature For Middle-Aged Guys
satire.summary: SAN JOSE, CA — In a recent update, Zoom added the ability for middle-aged men to apply a camera filter that gives them a full head of hair.
